Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.passkeys

Class PasskeySecondFactorLockoutFilter

java.lang.Object
org.springframework.web.filter.GenericFilterBean
org.springframework.web.filter.OncePerRequestFilter
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.passkeys.PasskeySecondFactorLockoutFilter
All Implemented Interfaces:
jakarta.servlet.Filter, org.springframework.beans.factory.Aware, org.springframework.beans.factory.BeanNameAware, org.springframework.beans.factory.DisposableBean, org.springframework.beans.factory.InitializingBean, org.springframework.context.EnvironmentAware, org.springframework.core.env.EnvironmentCapable, org.springframework.web.context.ServletContextAware
public class PasskeySecondFactorLockoutFilter extends org.springframework.web.filter.OncePerRequestFilter
Applies the second-factor lockout to a passkey that completes a second-factor step. It runs right before the WebAuthn authentication filter on POST /login/webauthn: when the session already holds a signed-in user (the password was presented, see MfaAuthorizationManager.isUser(org.springframework.security.core.Authentication)), the passkey is being used as that user's second factor, and while CheckSecondFactorLockoutUseCase reports the user's second factor locked (after too many failed codes of another factor) the request is answered 401 and the chain does not continue, so a passkey cannot be used to step around a lockout. A passkey used as the primary, passwordless sign-in (no user in the session) is not affected: there is no account to look up before the assertion is verified.

Failed passkey assertions are deliberately not counted as failed second-factor attempts: an assertion is a signature by a private key that never leaves the authenticator, over a fresh server challenge, so it cannot be guessed the way a six-digit code can, and counting the user's cancelled or failed ceremonies would only let them lock themselves out of their other factors.

It is not a bean: PasskeyChainCustomizer builds it (a Filter bean would also be registered by Spring Boot in the servlet container, outside the security chain).
